events.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) ruled out for Sunday night at Atlanta; Tyler Huntley starts
events.detail: Jesse Minter ruled Jackson out Friday after he missed every practice this week with the left ankle sprain from the Titans game. It is his first missed game of the season. Tyler Huntley starts; he was 2-0 as a fill-in starter last season and went 8 of 9 for 63 yards in relief against Tennessee. Minter would not commit to a Week 6 timeline vs. Cleveland. Zay Flowers (foot) was listed Questionable on the Ravens' Friday report.
events.so_what: Bench Jackson and pick up or start your QB2 now: this is a Sunday-night game, so there is no late swap if you wait. Huntley is a streaming option only in deeper formats; his legs keep a floor, but 4-pt pass TDs reward volume he will not supply. Downgrade Flowers a tier with Huntley throwing and a foot tag of his own.

source.label: ESPN: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson out; Huntley to start SNF vs. Falcons

events.headline: Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith (hamstrings) ruled out for London vs. Jacksonville; Hollywood Brown also out
events.detail: Philadelphia's final report ruled out Barkley, DeVonta Smith (second straight missed game), WR Hollywood Brown (ankle), C Drew Kendall and S Marcus Epps. With Tank Bigsby on IR, Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce are the backs. Dallas Goedert returns from his Week 2 knee injury. Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was limited Friday but carries no designation.
events.so_what: Shipley is a volume FLEX start this week. Three Eagles pass-catchers out concentrates targets on whoever is left, so the returning Goedert goes straight back into the TE slot in a format this shallow at the position. Wicks is the only healthy depth receiver and a one-week dart, not a FAAB target.

source.label: ESPN: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith among 5 Eagles ruled out vs. Jaguars

events.headline: D'Andre Swift (hip, knee) cleared, no designation for Sunday at Green Bay
events.detail: Swift went DNP Wednesday and limited Thursday, then came off the Bears' injury report entirely Friday. With Kyle Monangai ruled out, he is the lead back. He was benched in the third quarter last week after his second fumble of the season.
events.so_what: Start Swift as an RB2/FLEX on lead-back volume. The fumble benching is the one risk to the workload; Roschon Johnson is the only other back.

source.label: PFT: Bears rule Kyle Monangai out for Week 5

events.headline: Kyle Monangai (toe) ruled out at Green Bay, in a boot and week-to-week
events.detail: Ben Johnson ruled Monangai out Friday; the toe, not the thumb, is the real problem. He is in a boot and now week-to-week. Caleb Williams is Questionable after a limited Friday.
events.so_what: Bench Monangai. His week-to-week tag makes a short IR stash reasonable if you have the slot open, rather than burning one of 5 bench spots. D'Andre Swift takes the lead-back work.

source.label: PFT: Bears rule Kyle Monangai out for Week 5

events.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) ruled out vs. Giants; Terry McLaurin Questionable after first practice Friday
events.detail: Dan Quinn ruled out Diggs, Washington's leading receiver, after he missed Friday too. McLaurin practiced Friday for the first time this week and is Questionable; Quinn said he "looked good." Jayden Daniels (elbow) returns after two missed games. Marcus Mariota is out.
events.so_what: Diggs is a sit. McLaurin is a genuine coin-flip on one practice: if he is active Sunday morning, Daniels's return makes him a WR2/FLEX start, but have a same-window pivot since a hamstring re-tweak mid-game is the real risk.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Commanders vs. Giants Friday injury report

events.headline: Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins practice fully Friday but both listed Questionable vs. Miami
events.detail: Both Bengals receivers were full participants Friday and carry Questionable tags for Sunday at Miami. For Chase the full practice is the protocol step he needed; the remaining step is independent-neurologist clearance, which can land Saturday. Higgins went from two DNPs to full.
events.so_what: Pencil both in as starts: full Friday sessions are the strongest signal a Questionable tag can carry. Confirm Chase's protocol clearance before lock, and keep Dohnte Meyers as a deep-league pivot only.

source.label: Dolphins On SI: final Week 5 injury report

events.headline: Ashton Jeanty (ankle/foot) Questionable at New England after a Friday DNP
events.detail: Jeanty went full Wednesday, limited Thursday and did not practice Friday, and is Questionable. Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is Questionable on the Patriots side after three limited days. Raiders WRs Jalen Nailor and Dont'e Thornton Jr. are out. Brock Bowers practiced fully Friday with no designation.
events.so_what: Full, limited, DNP is the worst trend a Questionable can carry. Start him only if you have no comparable RB; otherwise the safer play is a bench RB. If you start him, confirm he is active before his game locks. Mike Washington Jr. is the handcuff and a viable one-week FLEX if Jeanty is inactive.

source.label: Raiders.com: Raiders-Patriots Week 5 injury report

events.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) Questionable vs. Vikings; Chris Olave and Tyler Shough carry no designation
events.detail: Kamara missed Wednesday, then practiced Thursday and Friday (limited on the official report) and is Questionable. Olave was upgraded to full Friday and has no game designation despite the foot issue added Thursday. Shough (left hand) practiced fully Thursday and Friday and is also off the report.
events.so_what: Kamara is a probable start; the back injury argues for a managed snap count, so treat him as an RB2/FLEX rather than a locked RB1. Olave is a normal start.

source.label: WWL/Audacy: Saints rule out three players; Kamara questionable

events.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) and Jordan Addison (hamstring) both Questionable at New Orleans
events.detail: Jefferson was limited all three days and is Questionable; he said Wednesday the plan is to play. Addison missed Wednesday, then was limited Thursday and Friday, and is also Questionable. Minnesota ruled out OT Christian Darrisaw (concussion). The Vikings are on bye in Week 6.
events.so_what: Start Jefferson; three limited days on an ankle he has said he will play through is a lean-yes. Addison is the shakier of the two and a FLEX at best. Both go on bye next week, so plan the Week 6 hole now.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Vikings final injury report, two out and five questionable

events.headline: CeeDee Lamb (quad) leaves Thursday's loss to Tampa Bay, tries one snap and exits again; Week 6 status unclear
events.detail: Lamb had 2 catches on 5 targets for 9 yards before going out in the fourth quarter of the 24-16 loss to the Buccaneers. He returned for one snap, appeared to be in discomfort, and later came back only for the failed two-point try. He was listed questionable to return. George Pickens caught 9 of 13 targets for 130 yards and a TD, and Ryan Flournoy had 3 catches for 90 yards. Dallas plays at Green Bay in Week 6, so Lamb has a full extra practice week before the next report.
events.so_what: Lamb's Week 5 points are banked. For Week 6, treat him as unresolved until the first Cowboys injury report: a quad that pulls him off the field twice is not a lineup fact either way. Pickens is a locked WR start with Lamb hobbled, and Flournoy is the speculative add if Lamb misses time.

source.label: NBC Sports: CeeDee Lamb questionable to return to TNF in Week 5

events.headline: Bucky Irving runs for 165 yards and a TD as Tampa Bay piles up 241 rushing yards behind rookie Jalon Daniels
events.detail: In the 24-16 Thursday win at Dallas, Irving had a career-best 21 carries for 165 yards and a rushing TD plus a receiving score. Kenneth Gainwell had 7 touches. Daniels, in his second start for the injured Baker Mayfield, went 19 of 25 for 189 yards and a TD with no turnovers and 23 rushing yards. Emeka Egbuka caught 6 of 9 targets for 38 yards and scored on a 14-yard run.
events.so_what: With a rookie QB, Tampa Bay leaned on the run, and Irving's 21-to-7 split over Gainwell is a lead-back role worth an RB2 start every week Mayfield sits. Daniels protected the ball but is not a fantasy start. Egbuka's 9 targets keep him a FLEX on volume even on a short-passing day.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Buccaneers-Cowboys Week 5 TNF live updates

events.headline: Mike Evans (ribs) DNP Thursday after a limited Wednesday; worked on a side field
events.detail: Evans did not practice Thursday for the 49ers after a limited session Wednesday, running at full speed on a side field during the open portion. He played through the same rib injury in Week 4 against Denver, catching 5 passes for 76 yards after a similar practice pattern. Friday's report sets his status for Sunday at Seattle.
events.so_what: The Week 4 precedent says this is a veteran managing reps rather than a setback, so plan to start him if he avoids an Out tag Friday. Have a Sunday-afternoon WR pivot in case the designation turns into a game-time decision.

source.label: NBC Sports: Mike Evans (ribs) does not practice on Thursday

events.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) returns to Giants practice as a limited participant Thursday
events.detail: Nabers was limited Thursday after missing Wednesday with a sore knee (Giants.com's Dan Salomone). He is back from last season's ACL and meniscus tears, and a full session Friday could keep a designation off him for Sunday against the Commanders.
events.so_what: Trending toward playing, so keep him in a WR slot unless Friday brings a step back. The knee history makes his snap share worth checking after the game rather than assuming a full workload.

source.label: RotoWire: Malik Nabers marked as limited Thursday

events.headline: D.J. Moore (shoulder) sits out Thursday's open practice, but Joe Brady says he will do everything to play Monday
events.detail: Moore was not seen in the media portion of Thursday's practice after reaggravating his shoulder. Joe Brady said Moore is going to do everything he can to play this week, and that if the receiver feels healthy enough he owes it to him to let him play. The Bills host the Rams on Monday night, which gives Moore extra days.
events.so_what: A Monday-night kickoff with an unresolved shoulder is the worst spot for lineup locks. If you have a Sunday alternative of similar value, start that one. Keon Coleman is the Bills receiver who picks up the snaps if Moore sits.

source.label: NBC Sports: DJ Moore (shoulder) not practicing Thursday

events.headline: Sean Payton takes play-calling back from Davis Webb starting Week 5 vs. the Chargers
events.detail: Payton confirmed Thursday that he will call the offensive plays Sunday, reversing February's handoff to OC Davis Webb. Webb keeps a significant game-planning and game-day role and may stay in Bo Nix's headset, per ESPN. Denver is 2-2 with a bottom-six offense in both yards and points. Seattle visits Denver the following Thursday.
events.so_what: A play-caller change is a usage shift the projections have not priced. Give Bo Nix and the Broncos' skill players a game before moving them up or down; two games in five days gives a fast read.

source.label: NBC Sports: Shocker: Sean Payton reclaims play-calling duties

events.headline: Michael Pittman Jr. aggravates his foot in practice and will miss multiple weeks
events.detail: Mike McCarthy said Pittman aggravated his left foot (plantar fasciitis, which already cost him Week 2) in Wednesday's practice, calling it a multiple-week injury. He will miss Sunday against the Colts, and IR is possible. He has 7 catches for 89 yards in three games. Roman Wilson and rookie Germie Bernard are expected to absorb the snaps.
events.so_what: With only 5 bench spots, holding Pittman costs a roster slot unless he goes to IR and you have it open. Roman Wilson is the speculative add, though a thin Steelers passing game caps his weekly ceiling.

source.label: ESPN: Steelers receiver Michael Pittman aggravates foot, out weeks

events.headline: Breece Hall (quad) remains week-to-week and trends toward another missed game; Braelon Allen keeps the lead role
events.detail: Aaron Glenn says Hall, who strained his quad against the Lions in Week 3, is still week-to-week, and he is trending toward missing Sunday against the Browns. Braelon Allen would carry another heavy workload.
events.so_what: Keep Hall benched until he strings practices together. Allen is a volume FLEX start while this lasts.

source.label: NBC Sports: Breece Hall (quad) remains week to week

events.headline: Tank Dell returns to Texans practice, opening his 21-day activation window
events.detail: Dell practiced Wednesday for the first time this regular season after opening the year on IR, recovering from the multi-ligament knee injury he suffered in December 2024. Houston now has 21 days to activate him or leave him on IR. No game date has been set.
events.so_what: Not a lineup option yet; he is a stash. A bench stash costs one of only five bench spots, so it is worth it only on a roster that can carry a no-points slot for two or three weeks.

source.label: Yahoo Sports NFL live updates, Oct. 7, 2026

events.headline: Jayden Daniels (elbow) practices in full Wednesday, on track to start vs. Giants; Mariota (MCL) avoids IR
events.detail: Daniels was a full participant Wednesday and Washington is aiming to start him Sunday against the Giants; he will wear a brace on his left arm. Marcus Mariota sprained his right MCL in London and will not go on IR, but did not practice. Dan Quinn had said Daniels needed a full practice week to play.
events.so_what: Still a forecast until Friday's report clears him, but a full Wednesday is the strongest signal yet. If he plays, his rushing is the konami premium that makes him a QB1; note his top two receivers both sat Wednesday (separate item), which caps the passing ceiling this week.

source.label: Yahoo Sports Week 5 injury report, Oct. 7, 2026

events.headline: Kyren Williams plays 70 snaps to Blake Corum's 13 with a career-high 13 targets in Rams win
events.detail: In the 24-20 comeback over the Eagles, Williams ran 16 times for 80 yards and two TDs and caught 10 of 13 targets for 67 yards. Corum played about 15% of snaps.
events.so_what: This is a workhorse role: every-down snaps, goal-line work and a passing-game share on top. Start him every week as an RB1. Corum is not a meaningful handcuff unless Williams gets hurt.

source.label: The Fantasy Footballers, Oct. 5-6, 2026

events.headline: Keon Coleman plays 78% of snaps and goes 6-116-1 after D.J. Moore's shoulder injury; Dalton Kincaid fades
events.detail: With Moore out of the Week 4 game, Coleman played 46 of 59 snaps (up from 48%) and ran 28 routes. Kincaid fell to 35 snaps and 20 routes for two targets as Buffalo leaned on three-wide sets.
events.so_what: Coleman is a starter-grade WR3/FLEX for as long as Moore sits, and a 34-yard TD shows the downfield role. Kincaid's route drop is the bigger warning: at a shallow TE position, 20 routes is not a startable floor.

source.label: The Fantasy Footballers, Oct. 6, 2026

events.headline: Ladd McConkey aggravates his foot at Seattle, called "week-to-week" by Jim Harbaugh
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 4 item. McConkey was active against the Seahawks but aggravated the same foot injury that had him questionable, played 24 snaps, failed to catch either of his two targets and was ruled out in the third quarter. Harbaugh called him "week-to-week" on Monday, while ESPN's Kris Rhim reported he may be closer to day-to-day. The first Chargers injury report comes Wednesday. Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris are Justin Herbert's top two wideouts if McConkey sits.
events.so_what: Not a fact you can set a lineup on yet: if he is healthy enough to practice Wednesday he is a FLEX, otherwise plan around him. Johnston is the main beneficiary of any absence; Harris is a speculative add only. The Chargers line is also falling apart (Joe Alt and Trevor Penning both hurt), which caps every Chargers pass catcher.

source.label: RotoWire, Oct. 5

events.headline: Tyreek Hill expected to sign "over the next few days," agent says; Chiefs among teams in talks
events.detail: Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Monday he anticipates Hill signing with a team within days. Kansas City reached out Sunday night after losing Tyquan Thornton (dislocated ankle, 12 to 16 weeks) and Rashee Rice (hamstring, possibly several weeks). Hill is recovering from the dislocated knee and torn ACL he suffered in Week 4 of 2025, and the Chiefs believe he is targeting a November return.
events.so_what: Nothing to start before November. If he lands in Kansas City he walks into a depleted receiver room with Mahomes, which makes him a bench stash worth a spot for anyone with room; anywhere else, wait for a practice before spending one. Rice holders should note a Hill signing would cap Rice's target share once both are healthy.

source.label: ESPN, Oct. 5

events.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) could miss several weeks; Tyquan Thornton out 12 to 16 weeks after ankle dislocation
events.detail: Rice pulled up on a first-quarter catch-and-run against the Raiders and did not return. Andy Reid called it a tweak, but The Athletic's Mike Silver reported Rice could be out several weeks. Kansas City has its bye in Week 5, so the first game he can miss is Week 6 against the Chargers. Thornton dislocated his ankle in the fourth quarter and needs surgery, with a possible late-season return.
events.so_what: Hold Rice through the bye and read the Week 6 practice reports; this is a bench stash, not a drop. With Thornton gone for months, the Chiefs' remaining receivers and tight ends absorb Mahomes' targets, so watch which one runs the most routes in Week 6.

source.label: NBC Sports, Oct. 4

events.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) won't play Week 5 vs. 49ers; Emanuel Wilson keeps the lead role
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 3 item. Mike Macdonald said Monday that Charbonnet will take team reps in practice this week but will not play against San Francisco, which points to Week 6 at the earliest. Jadarian Price is on IR until Week 8. Wilson handled 75% of the backfield carries in Sunday's win over the Chargers, with 81 rushing yards, three catches for 39 yards and two total TDs.
events.so_what: Wilson is a FLEX start again in Week 5 on volume and goal-line work. Charbonnet is a stash that turns into a committee around Week 6.

source.label: NBC Sports, Oct. 5
